evals.name: pr-description-docs
evals.prompt: the current branch adds the service guide for Contoso Queue (skeleton covering all five pillars) plus the entries in TOC.yml and service-guides/index.yml. write the PR description to PR.md, I'll open the PR with gh myself
evals.expected_output: One or two plain sentences on what the PR adds. No headings, no file list, no restated section names.
expectations: Says what the PR adds in at most two sentences
Does not restate the five pillar section names as a list
Contains nothing a reviewer could delete without losing information

evals.name: issue-title-and-links
evals.prompt: I'm assigned a feature about the KPI metrics (parent issue #3174). write a draft child issue to ISSUE.md for this topic: enable distinctCountColumns in the metrics backend so the dashboard gets accurate distinct counts (unique tenants, non-empty models). Only add a title and links to the docs into the draft issue. first line is the title. my research notes are in notes/
evals.expected_output: A title line, the two docs links, the parent reference. Nothing else.
expectations: Contains only a title, links, and at most a parent reference: no summary, options, steps or cost notes

evals.name: issue-comment-user-voice
evals.prompt:
can you write this infos as a comment for the github issue assigned to me, into COMMENT.md. just as comment

Question: Since the product is named Contoso health models, should our libraries, terraform modules, SDKs also be called like that?

Python and dotnet is currently CloudPulse, CLI and MCP is Contoso health models, PowerShell and Terraform module I would suggest to go with ContosoHealthModel(s)

maybe we can leave the SDK's and once we're GA release them under a new name?
evals.expected_output: The user's question and suggestions in their own words, typos fixed, a question plus 2-3 bullets. No heading, table, or added reasoning.
expectations: Keeps the user's question and suggestions without adding reasons, risks or a summary the user did not state
Reads as written by the user: first person, casual, no corporate phrasing

evals.name: email-new-role
evals.prompt: craft an e-mail to Dana Whitfield from Fabrikam that I will move into a new job on Dec 1 and Priya Raman takes over the health model rollout with them. add Priya to the CC. write it to EMAIL.md
evals.expected_output: A short casual note in plain sentences: heads up, new role on Dec 1, Priya takes over, thanks. No bullets, no bold.

must_not.label: corporate stock phrases
must_not.pattern: reach out|falls? through the cracks|truly appreciate|seamless|next steps|don't hesitate

expectations: Sounds like a person writing to a customer they know, not a template
Contains no claim or promise the prompt did not give

evals.name: readme-consumer-note
evals.prompt:
[review] MEDIUM: provider.bicep healthEndpoints output has a downstream consumer nobody knows about

tools/dashboard/deploy.ps1 parses healthEndpoints from the provider deployment. infra/provider/README.md does not mention this consumer; a refactor of the output will break the dashboard pipeline.

Suggested: add a one-line note in the README that healthEndpoints is parsed by tools/dashboard/deploy.ps1.

please add a note to infra/provider/README.md
evals.expected_output: One line that says tools/dashboard/deploy.ps1 parses healthEndpoints, so keep its shape. No new table or section essay. Short chat reply.
expectations: The added text tells a maintainer what breaks if they change healthEndpoints, in one or two lines

evals.name: code-doc-comment
evals.prompt: In src/shared/loaders.ts add loadEntityDependencies next to loadRelationships: it loads the child entities of a parent entity (list relationships for the model, keep the ones from the parent, fetch each child) and handles errors like the other loaders. Write its doc comment the way this file does it.
evals.expected_output: A one-line doc comment in the file's style, e.g. 'Loads the child entities of a parent entity. Notifies on API errors.'
expectations: The new doc comment matches the length and style of the file's existing one-line comments
The comment does not narrate callers, implementation steps, or history

evals.name: eli5-layout
evals.prompt: Context: a layered graph layout for health model entities now sorts the node ids once at the start so the same model always produces the same picture. You said: 'so DFS start order, Kahn queue seeding, and rank bucket order are fixed.' can you ELI5 that? make it very short ELI5, trying to avoid specialized terms
evals.expected_output: Two to four short sentences in everyday words, no algorithm or function names.
expectations: A non-programmer could follow it
Explains why sorting once makes the picture repeatable

evals.name: status-what-it-means
evals.prompt:
Facts: `npm run login` works and opens Edge with a separate profile for sign-in/MFA. Playwright's built-in `browser` fixture lives for a whole worker. Each test needs its own copied persistent profile and browser context. Our adapter tries to make `browser` test-scoped and Playwright rejects that override before launching anything, so the preflight and the minimal/rich E2E tests cannot run yet. I fix the adapter; the user does not need to do anything.

The user asks: and whats the issue still?
evals.expected_output: Consequence first in plain words: E2E is unfinished, sign-in works, tests can't run yet because Playwright rejects the setup, I'm fixing it, nothing to do for you.
expectations: The first sentence says in plain words what this means for the user
Says the user does not need to do anything
Avoids unexplained internals such as worker scope or fixture override

evals.name: docs-sentence-in-place
evals.prompt: In docs/health-models-guide.md, in the Operational excellence worked example (workload root with children: runtime, validation tests, bug reports), mention that workload health is not just whether the app is running, but whether it can provide the expected value.
evals.expected_output: One plain sentence added in the worked example. No contrast framing, no new paragraphs, no chat justification of placement.
expectations: Adds one or two sentences that tie the example's children to the value the workload provides

evals.name: adr-one-page
evals.prompt: Write ADR-0040 in docs/adr/ using docs/adr/0000-adr-template.md: Orleans ingress goes Azure Front Door -> internal load balancer -> pods, with no NGINX ingress controller. Each pod co-hosts ASP.NET Core (Kestrel, port 8080) and the Orleans silo (ADR-0003), so the in-process client routes grain calls with the silo's cluster view. Front Door (ADR-0020) already provides WAF, TLS, path routing and global anycast.
evals.expected_output: One page following the template: context bullets, the decision in one or two lines, consequence bullets, links to ADR-0003, ADR-0020 and docs.
expectations: States the decision in one or two sentences
Context and consequences are short bullets, not essay paragraphs
Contains no claims, numbers or alternatives the prompt and existing ADRs do not support

evals.name: issue-comment-hypothesis
evals.prompt:
Investigation result: in Windows High Contrast, the browser forces system colors (forced-colors: active) on borders, backgrounds and text, even over !important. Our .hc-* overrides only set background-color; health-state borders use hardcoded hex colors, so all states look the same. Possible fixes: forced-color-adjust: none on graph nodes, or @media (forced-colors: active) mapping states to system colors (LinkText, Highlight, CanvasText, GrayText). References: MDN forced-colors, MDN forced-color-adjust, W3C css-color-adjust-1.

write a comment with that information for the issue about the high contrast graph to COMMENT.md. make it suggestions and hypothesis, super brief, just as ideas to try out. references are the most important thing
evals.expected_output: About 6 lines: hypothesis framing, two ideas to try, the three references with links.
expectations: Frames the cause as a hypothesis, not an established finding
Lists the references prominently

evals.name: review-sloppy-readme
evals.prompt: clean up README.md: keep every fact, cut the filler and the AI-sounding phrasing. edit the file in place.
evals.expected_output: The README with every fact kept (30s checks, 3 failures before alerts, Slack/email, pulse.yaml, Python 3.12, make install, make dev, localhost:8080, PULSE_SLACK_WEBHOOK, MIT) and the marketing filler, emoji and em dashes gone.
expectations: Adds no new claims or features that the original did not state

evals.name: readme-from-code
evals.expected_output: A short README: one-line purpose, how to run it with GRAFANA_TOKEN/GRAFANA_URL, the options (--url, --out, --folder, --no-commit), what it writes and commits, exit code 2 without a token.
expectations: Every option and environment variable described matches the code; nothing is invented (no install steps, flags or behaviors the code lacks)
Contains no sentence that only praises the tool or restates another sentence

evals.name: investigation-summary
evals.prompt: summarize the checkout latency investigation from notes/investigation.md for the team channel. write it to SUMMARY.md
evals.expected_output: Cause first (marketing email -> inventory-service at HPA max -> checkout held DB transactions during the inventory call -> pool exhausted), when it recovered, follow-ups with owners. No dead-end narration.
expectations: The first sentence or two state the cause and impact
Lists the follow-ups with their owners
Contains no claim that the notes do not support

evals.name: explain-module
evals.prompt: I'm new here. how does src/cache/ttl_cache.py behave when an entry is older than ttl? answer here in chat
evals.expected_output: Answer first: between ttl and stale_ttl it returns the stale value and starts one background refresh; after stale_ttl (or missing) the caller loads synchronously. Mention that refresh errors are swallowed so the stale value stays.
expectations: The first sentence answers the question
Mentions that a failed background refresh is ignored and the old value keeps being served until stale_ttl
Contains no filler such as a closing summary or an offer of further help
